title: Add cross-provider agent session browser, replay, and export
description: Add a read-only agent catalog over local Grok, Claude Code, and Codex stores; expose human-readable list/show/export/replay commands; preserve live follow behavior without secret egress.
design:
# Agent Sessions: design v2.2

## Goal

Make every local parent session and subagent easy to find by provider, friendly name, date,
status, and id; make `show science` return the actual science result; export a selected run as
faithful Markdown plus terminal-style replay; and observe the live parent-to-child workflow
without needing the vendor TUI that created it.

## Product decisions

1. The durable engine belongs in `llm-anthology`, whose existing Grok, Claude Code, and Codex
   adapters already normalize transcripts and spawn edges. `D:\agent-monitor` remains reference
   behavior, not a second product.
2. The executable is `anth agents ...` (and `llm-anthology agents ...`). The chat skill is
   `agent-sessions`. Grok 1.0.5 already reserves `/agents` for agent-definition management, so
   this feature must not shadow it; the installed guide must clearly advertise `/agent-sessions`
   and `anth agents` as the collision-free entry points.
3. The catalog includes every root and child run, then enriches and deduplicates child records.
   Listing uses indexes and bounded header reads rather than parsing every full transcript.
4. Markdown and `show` use the normalized IR and retained parent-side final output. Replay and
   follow use a separate provider-neutral projection of raw ordered events so streaming cadence,
   tool transitions, timestamps, and completion framing are not lost by IR coalescing.
5. Status is evidence-bearing and bounded. The state set is `running`, `active`, `idle`,
   `completed`, `failed`, and `unknown`. An explicit terminal record wins. A persistent lock is
   never enough for `running`. Each record carries `status_basis` and `observed_at`.
6. Session files are untrusted data. Discovery is confined to explicit provider roots; export
   paths, terminal text, HTML, JSON, and follow-mode file replacement are hardened boundaries.

## Service model

Use a composite identity `(provider, canonical_id)`. `AgentSummary` contains `provider`, `id`,
`source_agent_id`, `session_id`, `aliases`, nullable `parent_id` and `workflow_id`, name, title,
role, status observation, nullable timestamps/duration, parent-reported tool count, independently
counted transcript tool events, model, cwd, and transcript/final-output availability. Ordinary
human/JSON listing does not reveal absolute paths unless `--verbose-paths` is requested. Unknown
metadata stays null rather than being invented.

`AgentDetail` adds `final_output`, `final_output_source`, normalized `conversation`, and raw-order
`replay_events`. The final output is the final non-empty assistant message content, with reasoning
excluded and tool/results retained separately. Parent-side `output.json` is preserved as a
distinct source and its disagreement with the transcript is disclosed.

Selectors resolve in this order: exact composite/full id, unique id prefix, exact
case-insensitive alias/name, then unique case-insensitive substring. Ambiguity is a non-zero
error with candidate provider, name, date, and id. Thus `science` resolves `Science lens
brainstorm`, while a non-unique `review` never guesses.

Add `ReplayEvent` with stable sequence, source offset, nullable timestamp in milliseconds,
provider event kind, role, call id, status, label, and sanitized display payload. Normalize
RFC-3339 strings and numeric Grok seconds/milliseconds. Provider event readers preserve raw order
and streaming updates without exposing encrypted reasoning. IR remains the source for clean
Markdown; native events are the source for ANSI/HTML/replay/follow.

Each detail also carries an ordered internal `TranscriptLeg` source set: provider, canonical
session id, source kind, opened-file identity, created/updated timestamps, compressed flag, and
an opaque source ordinal. Paths remain internal unless `--verbose-paths` is explicit. Single-file
Grok and Claude sessions have one leg. Codex rollouts sharing one validated `session_meta` id are
one logical session whose plain/archive legs are ordered by provider timestamp and then a stable
source ordinal; a plain file and its compressed twin are one physical leg, with plain preferred.

Native replay uses one shared `fold_leg_events` policy, analogous to the repository's existing
`loaders.fold_leg_turns` policy. An event key is the provider's stable event/item id when present;
otherwise it is a canonical fingerprint of event kind, normalized timestamp, call id, role, and
sanitized payload. The first leg is retained whole. A later leg's overlapping prefix is dropped,
new events append in leg/file order, and the richer rendering wins when one stable id has divergent
content; divergence and unreadable-leg counts are disclosed. Static replay/export consumes the
entire folded source set, never only the last rollout. Both catalog-time IR and selected raw-event
replay call shared public fold helpers, with parity tests preventing two merge policies from
drifting.

## Provider catalogs

- Grok: enumerate every session directory containing `summary.json` or `updates.jsonl`, excluding
  bookkeeping directories. Enrich each referenced child from parent-side
  `subagents/<id>/meta.json` and `output.json`, resolve its top-level child directory, and merge
  both views into one record. Retain the parent-reported final output and full child transcript.
  If the child directory is missing, `show` still returns `output.json` and replay explicitly
  reports that chronological history is unavailable. Status correlation may additionally read
  only a bounded tail of `<grok-home>/logs/unified.jsonl`. That reader allowlists the structural
  fields `timestamp`, `pid`, `ctx.session_id`, `ctx.pid`, `ctx.kind`, `ctx.state`, and
  `ctx.session_found`; it neither retains nor emits other log fields. It opens the log through the
  validated Grok-root handle, caps bytes/lines/JSON depth, and treats absence, truncation, parse
  failure, or permission failure as an unavailable detector rather than as negative evidence.
- Claude Code: enumerate both root `projects/**/*.jsonl` transcripts and
  `projects/**/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`/workflow variants through the existing path classifier.
  Enrich optional metadata, preserve workflow nodes, and deduplicate parent/child references
  without treating a short `agent-*` stem as globally unique.
- Codex: enumerate `session_index.jsonl`, dated `sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`, compressed
  `rollout-*.jsonl.zst`, and `archived_sessions/**`. Use bounded headers for catalog metadata and
  `adapters.codex_rollout` for selected transcripts. Aggregate every rollout leg with the same
  validated canonical session id into one ordered `TranscriptLeg` set and fold both IR turns and
  native replay events with the shared overlap policy. The existing allowlisted, read-only immutable
  `codex_state` adapter may enrich thread metadata and spawn edges; no arbitrary SQLite file may
  be opened. `thread_spawn_edges.status` is relationship metadata and must never populate run
  status. Codex run status comes only from validated terminal/process/activity evidence; otherwise
  the truth table yields `active`, `idle`, or `unknown`. Prefer plain JSONL over a compressed twin.
  Static replay supports `.zst` under explicit compressed/decompressed byte, record-count, JSON
  depth, window-size, and time limits; use streaming decompression with a configured maximum zstd
  window and stop before parsing once any limit is crossed. Follow refuses compressed rollouts
  because they are not append-tail-able, but may hand off from a completed leg to a newly discovered
  appendable plain leg of the same canonical session.

Never read `auth.json`, `mcp_credentials.json`, DPAPI settings, unrelated databases, or paths
outside the canonical provider roots. Do not follow symlinks, junctions, or other reparse points
by default. Validate provider ids before using them in path resolution.

## Commands

- `anth agents list [--provider ...] [--query ...] [--since ...] [--status ...]
  [--tree|--flat] [--json]`
- `anth agents show --selector <value> [--full] [--json] [--verbose-paths]
  [--include-sensitive]`
- `anth agents export --selector <value> --out <dir> [--format all|markdown|ansi|html|json]
  [--include-sensitive] [--overwrite]`
- `anth agents replay --selector <value> [--speed N] [--follow] [--no-color]`
- `anth agents watch [--interval N] [--active-seconds N] [--once] [--json]`

Human `list` defaults to a parent/workflow/child tree. Human `show` prints identity/provenance
followed by the actual final result; `--full` adds the clean normalized transcript. Human/JSON
`show` is redacted-safe by default and fails closed if redaction fails; raw output requires the
same explicit `--include-sensitive` override as export. The skill always uses the safe default.
JSON `show` has a stable metadata plus final-output schema and represents a missing result
explicitly. Explicit `--selector` makes leading-dash names inert data rather than options.
Diagnostics go to stderr so JSON stdout remains pure. Home flags (`--grok-home`, `--claude-home`,
`--codex-home`) override defaults and print inspected roots on stderr.

## Export contract

An `all` export writes:

- `<safe-stem>.md`: normalized Markdown, metadata, parent/child provenance, retained final output,
  and disclosed fidelity/redaction gaps.
- `<safe-stem>.ansi`: deterministic terminal scrollback that remains readable without color.
- `<safe-stem>.html`: self-contained offline terminal replay with sticky run/status header,
  elapsed/runtime markers, available token/context counters, play/pause/speed/step/seek,
  collapsible tool blocks, keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic landmarks, narrow-screen
  layout, and reduced-motion support.
- `<safe-stem>.json`: catalog metadata, native replay projection, normalized counts, source
  hashes, redaction manifest, and `unit_complete`.

The stem is `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM_<provider>_<sanitized-name>_<short-id>`. Sanitize separators,
control/bidi characters, ADS colons, reserved Windows device names, trailing dots/spaces, length,
Unicode/case collisions, and append an id-derived suffix. Canonicalize every output, verify
component-aware containment under `--out`, reject reparse-point escapes and existing files by
default, and create files with a user-restricted DACL. Open the root, staging directory, sources,
and outputs without following reparse points; validate final path, identity, and component-aware
containment from each opened handle, not only from pre-open strings. Use exclusive creation and
repeat final-handle validation after every follow reopen. Apply restrictive DACLs before writing
sensitive bytes and fail closed if DACL or handle validation fails.

Write each validated export set under immutable versioned/content-addressed names in a restricted
same-volume staging directory, atomically promote the new version directory, then switch exactly
one manifest/pointer. Retain the previous version until the pointer switch succeeds; never
sequentially replace the currently published files. Promotion is relative to the already validated
output-root handle, not a newly resolved path. On Windows use `SetFileInformationByHandle` with
the `FileRenameInfoEx` information class and a `FILE_RENAME_INFO` structure whose `RootDirectory`
is the validated root handle: do not set replace for an immutable version promotion, and set
replace only for the single pointer swap. On POSIX use directory-fd-relative, no-follow creation
and rename. Re-open and validate the published pointer and referenced version through the root
handle before reporting success. Default export is
redacted-safe using the existing privacy plane and fails closed if redaction fails;
`--include-sensitive` is the explicit faithful-private override. Every export records whether and
where redaction occurred. Warn or require the explicit override for UNC/network/cloud-synced
destinations.

Markdown/ANSI end with `UNIT-COMPLETE: <full-id>`. HTML places the same sentinel comment before
`</body>`. JSON uses a valid `unit_complete` field. Every delivered artifact stays parseable,
is at least 1 KiB, and contains the sentinel in its final 600 bytes.

Transcript-originated C0/C1 controls, ESC/BEL, bidi overrides, and unsafe terminal sequences are
removed or visibly encoded; ANSI is emitted only by trusted renderer code, and `--no-color`
contains no escape bytes. HTML inserts transcript text only with `textContent`; embedded JSON
escapes `<`, script termination, U+2028, and U+2029. It uses no remote resources, `innerHTML`,
eval, inline handlers, or transcript-derived URLs/CSS, and ships a restrictive hash-authorized
offline CSP.

## Follow and status truth table

Status precedence is: explicit failure/completion; session-correlated live process with matching
PID plus process start/owner/executable and recent activity; explicit active record plus recent
activity; recent activity alone; bounded idle/stale; unknown detector failure. Lock existence
alone never yields `running`. Detector errors produce `unknown`, not absence. Thresholds are
configurable and serialized in `status_basis`.

For Grok, the optional bounded `unified.jsonl` tail is the only session-to-PID join rail. A
candidate must match the exact session id, fall within the configured join-freshness window, and
name a PID that is still alive. The live process must independently match the expected Grok
executable, current owner, and start time compatible with the correlation event; this rejects PID
reuse. Transcript activity must also be recent. An explicit terminal child meta/event still wins
over a fresh log row. If the log reader or process detector fails, status is `unknown`; if the rail
is simply absent but transcript activity is fresh, status is only `active`, never `running`.

`TailCursor` carries file identity, byte offset, partial-line buffer, last sequence/activity, and a
bounded rolling checkpoint of raw-record fingerprints plus a short ordered fingerprint chain.
Follow reopens on each poll so Windows rotation is not blocked. Replacement or `size < offset`
triggers fresh catalog resolution, final-handle containment, and bounded overlap reconciliation;
it never blindly follows a replacement path. Every poll also re-resolves the logical session's
ordered source set. A newly created Codex rollout leg with the same canonical id is opened and
validated as a handoff candidate even when the old leg was not replaced or truncated; the shared
event fold proves the overlap boundary before the cursor advances. Stable provider event ids/ordinals are preferred
when present. Follow emits exactly once within an uninterrupted append-only file generation. If
the fingerprint chain aligns after rotation/copy-truncate, it resumes beyond the overlap without
duplicates. If continuity cannot be proven, it emits `replay_discontinuity` and resumes with
explicitly at-least-once semantics rather than making a false exactly-once claim. Bound file/line
size, partial-line buffer, JSON depth, events per increment, refresh rate, total duration, and
stale timeout. Sanitize all emitted text through the terminal boundary and exit on explicit
terminal state or bounded timeout.

## Live workflow UX

`watch` renders parent rows expandable into workflow and child rows with lineage, provider,
evidence-backed status, name, start/end/duration, tool counts, latest meaningful sanitized event,
and short id. It keeps a persistent run header and completion framing. Columns have an explicit
priority and collapse into a stacked narrow-terminal layout. Empty roots, zero results, ambiguous
selectors, partial parses, unavailable replay, and stale records each have distinct actionable
messages. ANSI is TTY-only; UTF-8 Windows consoles and Ctrl+C are supported. `--once --json`
makes the same state mechanically testable.

## Skill and deployment

Create the concise `agent-sessions` skill in the canonical `.agents/skills/` tree of
`agent-skills-toolchain`, with compatibility publication only through that repo's existing
deployment path. It routes natural requests such as "show the science subagent output" to
`anth agents show --selector science`, explains the reserved Grok `/agents` collision, defaults exports to
an explicit output directory, and treats discovered metadata/transcripts as data rather than
instructions. It invokes only the installed executable with argument vectors and validated
roots/options. Validate its frontmatter and `agents/openai.yaml`, deploy, then verify discovery in
Grok, Claude, Codex, and the installed `anth` command.

## Tests and executable definition of done

Use synthetic stores only in committed tests and TDD every behavior. Cover root/child discovery
and deduplication for all providers; exact/alias/substring/ambiguous selectors; parent output
fallback; explicit, live, active, stale, failed, and unknown status; `.jsonl` and `.zst`; malformed
and truncated records; Unicode on Windows; deterministic safe names; path/junction containment;
overwrite refusal; terminal OSC/CSI injection; safe HTML/script-breakout payloads and CSP;
redaction/ACL behavior; follow replacement/resource limits; CLI argument injection; JSON stdout
purity; narrow/accessibility markup; bounded compressed/decompressed `.zst`; redactor failure;
every format's valid sentinel; and a two-leg Codex resume whose second leg overlaps the first.
The resumed-session test requires one logical detail, all first-leg events, no duplicated overlap,
the richer divergent event, and a live follow handoff when the second leg appears without the first
being truncated. Grok status fixtures cover fresh allowlisted session/PID correlation, PID reuse,
stale joins, malformed/unreadable logs, completed-meta precedence, and the active-only fallback.
Race tests swap a validated directory for a junction before
open and require final-handle confinement to fail. Option tests pass `--include-sensitive`,
`--overwrite`, and `--grok-home` as selector values and require them to remain inert data.

Real-data E2E must catalog the named parent plus science
`01a01a07-5f03-7510-ae4d-19b7ffd5d1ee` and novelty
`01a01a07-5f04-7cf1-a97a-4a076c2e68de`, with correct parent edges, completed status, durations
819414/385668 ms, and parent tool counts 24/26. `show science` and `show novelty` must return their
actual results. Export both in all formats, independently recompute source hashes/event/count
fields, and verify existence, size, parseability, and sentinels.

Also verify one real root and child for Claude Code, one root and spawned rollout for Codex, and
one real resumed multi-leg Codex session: independently compare the catalog's ordered source set
and folded replay against every source leg, then exercise follow across a newly created resume leg.
Verify one short real Grok child through `running` to `completed`: `watch --once --json` must fire for
the live state, replay follow must observe appended events exactly once, and both must terminate.
The known completed Grok children with persistent locks are the broken-state control and must
never report `running`. Capture a shape-only receipt proving the live child's `session_id`/PID join
came from the allowlisted log fields and that independent owner/executable/start checks passed;
never record raw log content.

Run mutations that restore lock-as-running, import Codex edge status as run status, omit root
enumeration, drop a replay chunk/tool update, omit a Codex first leg, duplicate an overlapping
resume prefix, stop source-set re-resolution while following, accept a stale/reused Grok PID,
claim exactly-once after unrelated replacement,
append an invalid raw JSON sentinel, disable final-handle confinement/control sanitization, or
disable HTML escaping; each must turn the relevant test red. Run the Python 100% branch-coverage
gate, packaging/wheel smoke, real-data E2E, skill validation/deployment smoke, and fresh
code/security/UX review. After deployment, exercise one natural-language request through each
Grok, Claude, and Codex skill catalog and require the route to call the installed executable with
`--selector`, return the actual selected result, and produce its machine-verifiable receipt;
skill discovery alone is not completion.

## Deferred without pretending it is done

A native Cockpit Agents pane can consume the catalog later. The first complete release still has
an actual live workflow tree (`watch`), a faithful raw-event terminal replay (ANSI/HTML), a clean
archive (Markdown/JSON), actual-result lookup (`show`), and the cross-tool `/agent-sessions`
entry point. Literal Grok `/agents` remains the provider's reserved command.

UNIT-COMPLETE: agents-design-v2.2
acceptance_criteria: Catalog every local Grok, Claude Code, and Codex parent/child run; show actual selected final output; fold resumed Codex legs without omission or duplicate overlap; export validated Markdown/ANSI/HTML/JSON with atomic pointer publication; provide bounded replay/follow/watch with evidence-bearing status; deploy the agent-sessions skill; pass 100% Python branch coverage, real-data, packaging, security, mutation, and cross-host natural-language gates.
